context: Adjectives ending in -e don't change in the feminine: un pull rouge, une robe rouge.
Same sound in both genders; plural adds -s: des yeux bleus.
In the feminine you hear the final t: une pomme verte.
'Le gilet jaune' (yellow vest) became the name of a 2018 protest movement.
'Un café noir' = black coffee.
Irregular feminine: blanc → blanche.
The s becomes audible in the feminine: une voiture grise.
These come from nouns (an orange, a chestnut), so they never change: des chaussures marron.
'Voir la vie en rose' = to see life through rose-tinted glasses.
Placed BEFORE the noun: une grande maison, un petit chat.
Before a masculine vowel: 'un bel homme'. Also placed before the noun.
Vieux → vieille (f) → 'un vieil ami' before a vowel.
Feminine: bonne, mauvaise. Both go before the noun: un bon film.
Before a masculine vowel: 'un nouvel appartement'.
'C'est facile !' Most adjectives go AFTER the noun: un exercice facile.
'Bon marché' never changes. 'Pas cher' is more common in speech.
'Je suis contente' (f). 'Heureux/heureuse' = happy in a deeper sense.
'Je suis fatigué(e)', 'je suis malade'.

front: De quelle couleur est ta voiture ?
context: 'De quelle couleur…?' = what color…? Answer: 'Elle est rouge.'
Colors go AFTER the noun: une voiture rouge (never 'une rouge voiture').
Short, common adjectives go before the noun (BAGS: Beauty, Age, Goodness, Size): joli, petit, grand, jeune…

front: Elle porte une robe noire et des chaussures blanches.
pronunciation: [el port ün rob NWAHR ay day shoh-sür BLAHNSH]
back: She's wearing a black dress and white shoes.
context: Agreement: robe (f) → noire; chaussures (f pl) → blanches.

front: Mon frère est grand et sportif.
back: My brother is tall and sporty.
context: Feminine of -if adjectives: -ive. 'Ma sœur est sportive.'
Gentil → gentille (double l). Don't confuse it with 'gentle'.
Long → longue in the feminine. 'Trop' = too, too much.
'Cette' (f) / 'ce' (m) / 'cet' (m before a vowel) = this.
Plural adjectives add -s (silent in speech).
Weather uses 'il fait': il fait beau, il fait chaud, il fait froid.

front: Ce n'est pas cher du tout !
context: 'Pas du tout' = not at all.

front: Mon appartement est petit mais lumineux.
back: My apartment is small but bright.
context: 'Lumineux' (full of light) is a key word in French apartment listings.
